reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the cap is keyed to "Fees," defined in 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so a 12-month look-back captures no subscription or services charges — an illusory cap well below the fallback's 12 months' fees (and below 6 months), i.e. walk-away territory rather than an acceptable fallback.

Redline is targeted and minimal: it edits only the cap basis in the existing sentence (greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding 12 months, or USD 1,000,000) and leaves mutuality, the indirect-damages exclusion in 21.2 and the Excluded Claims carve-outs in 21.3 untouched, consistent with the redline guidance.

Comment is accurate and correctly cites the playbook position, explains the illusory-Fees defect, and confirms indemnification, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud remain outside the cap.

Rationale properly notes that the other elements (mutual cap, carve-out set, payment obligations not treated as damages) already match the preferred position, so no duplicate or over-flagging of compliant sub-elements; deterministic checks all pass and the 0.327 change ratio is justified by the required change of cap basis.
